findings.summary: The words that hand a conversation to a person are matched as substrings, so ordinary sentences silence the bot for seven days.
findings.failure: A customer types 你们这是人工智能吗？ -- Chinese for "is this an AI?", and the likeliest first question anybody asks an AI demo. 人工智能 contains 人工, so the bot sends the transfer line and goes mute until somebody opens the console or the customer types menu. 'I bought it from your agent last week' and 'is this suitable for human resources teams?' do the same, and realestate's own persona (realestate.json:16,31) instructs the bot to offer the word agent while having no tools, so the keyword list is its only path. The docstring asserted 人工 was not a fragment of anything a customer says; that premise was false and untested.

findings.summary: Six paths let the bot speak while a person holds the conversation, and what they send are the lines that announce there is a bot.
findings.failure: The handover guard sits inside _handle_text_message; five paths return before it -- an unsupported message type, a voice note that will not transcribe, a photo or document that will not download, and the daily cap. Each sends its canned apology over the top of whoever is typing on the console. The sixth is worse: notify._send has no handover check, so a push queued by an order placed a minute earlier fires during the handover and interrupts the human with 'your order is on its way'. The commit message claimed the bot sends 'nothing at all, not even an apology'; those five strings are the apologies.
